rows: Most monkeys and apes have three kinds of cone, as you do, and some New World monkeys have only two or fewer. Owl monkeys and bushbabies have one kind, so they see no colour.
A macaque can resolve about 26 cycles per degree in its best test, close to yours. Marmoset foveas are estimated near 30. We blur the picture to a lower figure.
Most monkeys and apes have a clear central fovea. Owl monkeys have only a rudimentary one, and the fovea of a squirrel monkey is clearly seen.
Owl monkeys and bushbabies are active at night, and macaques and marmosets by day. The owl monkey has a fully nocturnal retina.
The field of view, the sharp centre, the dim-light lift and the colour mapping are the app's guesses. No record gave these numbers for a monkey.

claims.how: The three-cone count for macaques supports a three-class colour model, though the matrix itself is the app's stand-in.
